research_mode: official Home Office accredited statistics; fail-closed limitations; no parcel score, candidate value or business result

sources.name: Neighbourhood policing baseline
verified_claims: The 31 March 2025 neighbourhood policing baseline was 17,175 FTE officers and PCSOs.
limitations: The baseline is a programme measure and excludes parcel-level deployment information.

sources.name: Neighbourhood policing total
verified_claims: There were 20,989 FTE personnel in neighbourhood policing roles or in training for such roles at 31 March 2026.
limitations: The total combines deployed and training personnel and cannot indicate exact-address coverage.

sources.name: Neighbourhood police officers
verified_claims: The neighbourhood policing total included 14,599 FTE police officers, of whom 350 FTE were in training.
limitations: Personnel in training may not yet be operationally deployed, so the figure is not parcel evidence.

sources.name: Neighbourhood PCSOs
verified_claims: The neighbourhood policing total included 6,390 FTE PCSOs, of whom 122 FTE were in training.
limitations: Training and in-post counts cannot be treated as local presence at a property.

sources.name: Neighbourhood policing growth
verified_claims: Neighbourhood policing personnel grew by 3,814 FTE, or 22.2%, above the March 2025 baseline.
limitations: Programme growth is an aggregate and does not map personnel to individual parcels.

sources.name: Neighbourhood officer growth
verified_claims: Police officers accounted for 3,494 FTE, or 91.6%, of neighbourhood policing growth.
limitations: The share of programme growth does not establish local service outcomes.

sources.name: Neighbourhood PCSO growth
verified_claims: PCSOs accounted for 319 FTE, or 8.4%, of neighbourhood policing growth.
limitations: The aggregate share cannot identify the location or timing of deployment.

sources.name: Neighbourhood programme target
verified_claims: The updated year-one neighbourhood policing growth target was 3,011 FTE.
limitations: A programme target is not evidence that any specific parcel received additional policing.

sources.name: Neighbourhood target achievement
verified_claims: Total neighbourhood policing growth reached 126.7% of the updated year-one target.
limitations: Target achievement does not demonstrate uniform deployment or local safety effects.

sources.name: Officer target achievement
verified_claims: Neighbourhood police officer growth reached 133.7% of the officer target.
limitations: An aggregate target ratio cannot be translated into a parcel-level candidate.

sources.name: PCSO target achievement
verified_claims: Neighbourhood PCSO growth reached 80.6% of the PCSO target.
limitations: The programme ratio does not measure service coverage around a property.

sources.name: Neighbourhood absence exclusion
verified_claims: Neighbourhood policing programme figures exclude employees on long-term absence.
limitations: The exclusion means the figures are not identical to all workforce totals and require cautious comparison.

sources.name: Neighbourhood BTP exclusion
verified_claims: Neighbourhood policing programme figures exclude British Transport Police.
limitations: The scope exclusion prevents treating the figures as all-policing coverage for every location.

sources.name: Neighbourhood personnel in role
verified_claims: There were 20,517 FTE officers and PCSOs recorded in neighbourhood policing roles excluding those still in training.
limitations: A role snapshot does not show shift patterns, patrol intensity or parcel-level presence.

sources.name: Neighbourhood direct recruits
verified_claims: Of personnel in neighbourhood policing roles excluding trainees, 1,206 FTE, or 5.9%, were standard direct recruits since April 2025.
limitations: Recruitment route does not indicate effectiveness or risk at an address.

sources.name: Neighbourhood direct-recruit officers
verified_claims: There were 472 FTE direct-recruit officers, equal to 3.3% of neighbourhood police officers in role.
limitations: The category is a workforce characteristic, not local incident evidence.

sources.name: Neighbourhood direct-recruit PCSOs
verified_claims: There were 734 FTE direct-recruit PCSOs, equal to 11.7% of neighbourhood PCSOs in role.
limitations: The category cannot be spatially attributed to a parcel.

sources.name: Neighbourhood service 1 to 5 years
verified_claims: A 27.7% share of neighbourhood officers and PCSOs had one to less than five years of service.
limitations: Experience distribution is an aggregate workforce measure and not a local safety outcome.

sources.name: Neighbourhood service 5 to 10 years
verified_claims: A 28.5% share of neighbourhood officers and PCSOs had five to less than ten years of service.
limitations: Service-band shares cannot identify capability at a specific address.

sources.name: Neighbourhood service under one year
verified_claims: A 5.8% share of neighbourhood officers and PCSOs had less than one year of service.
limitations: A national experience share is not parcel-level evidence.

sources.name: Neighbourhood under-ten-years comparison
verified_claims: A 62.1% share of neighbourhood officers and PCSOs had less than ten years of service, compared with 53.6% across all officers and PCSOs.
limitations: The comparison is descriptive and does not measure operational quality at a location.

sources.name: Neighbourhood service 20 to 25 years
verified_claims: A 11.2% share of neighbourhood personnel had 20 to less than 25 years of service, compared with 16.7% across all officers and PCSOs.
limitations: Experience-band differences cannot be converted into a parcel risk score.

sources.name: Neighbourhood service 25 to 30 years
verified_claims: A 3.3% share of neighbourhood personnel had 25 to less than 30 years of service, compared with 6.9% across all officers and PCSOs.
limitations: The aggregate comparison gives no exact-address coverage evidence.

sources.name: Neighbourhood constable share
verified_claims: Constables accounted for 80.2% of neighbourhood police officers.
limitations: Rank composition is organisational information and not a local outcome measure.

sources.name: Neighbourhood sergeant share
verified_claims: Sergeants accounted for 15.2% of neighbourhood police officers.
limitations: Rank share cannot identify supervision or patrol conditions at a parcel.

sources.name: Neighbourhood inspector share
verified_claims: Inspectors accounted for 4.2% of neighbourhood police officers.
limitations: The national proportion cannot establish local command availability.

sources.name: Neighbourhood chief-inspector share
verified_claims: Chief inspectors accounted for 0.3% of neighbourhood police officers.
limitations: The rank proportion is not parcel-level public-safety evidence.

sources.name: Neighbourhood superintendent share
verified_claims: Superintendents accounted for 0.04% of neighbourhood police officers.
limitations: A very small national rank share cannot support exact-address inference.

sources.name: Neighbourhood senior-rank scope
verified_claims: No neighbourhood police officers were recorded at chief superintendent or chief officer rank.
limitations: The absence reflects function coding and does not imply missing local command arrangements.

sources.name: Officers with under five years service
verified_claims: There were 43,525 police officers with less than five years of service, equal to 29.4% of officers on a headcount basis.
limitations: Length-of-service data are workforce characteristics, not parcel safety measures.
